column1:
Clive is a fundamentally demanding character who requires good defence from the player to
find the perfect opening for a heat engager. All his tough pressure and real deal comes from his
heat and the notorious "H u1+2" string (rekka as H-DOPE says). Clive also has good heat engagers that synergise with his heat, like "1+2", "f+2,2,2" and "SS+2,1". Moving on, Clive also has good variety to his lows, with "d1", "FC df+2" and "db4" being his best, and "FC df+2" 50/50ing with his "WS3" (i19/i20). This character also offers good pokes with "df1" and "1,1", a decent counterhit game with "2,2,1" and "b4", and strong sidestepping and backdashing capability. Like every character in this game, Clive has a stance with good options like "PHX 2" and "PHX 4" that set up good mind games, and "H PHX 2,1+2" / "PHX 3,2" which in heat is the best value for damage mix-up.

At a very low level, Clive feels very easy because not only are his combos not execution-heavy, but opponents are prone to making mistakes and having poor defence, which helps Clive find his opening and rush them down while in heat, leading to fast round wins. However, during the lifespan of Tekken 8, Clive got hit hard by nerfs on his win-conditioning moves. This character always played around his heat and the rekka string, so the player had to condition the opponent to respect it in order to go for the best value for damage mixup "H PHX 2,1+2" / "PHX 3,2". Now it's very difficult for this character to find damage because of the rekka being too unforgiving, heat consumption, and damage on win condition. Great Clive players like "Crescent" always have a way to play the rekka perfectly and adapt to the opponent's defence, making it a huge mental stack for them. So Clive is all about defence at first and then unleashing good rekka+stance mixups.
Outside of heat Clive feels like a Tekken 7 character
